title: TT-core Mirror adapter bank
hypothesis: For adapters whose task variation lies in a low-dimensional symmetry of one shared TT core, a per-task Mirror angle can replace independent task-specific TT cores with lower serialized bytes; LoRETTA independent factors and generic PCA are controls.
physical_object: shared TT cores for 16×16 linear adapters, with rank-2 bonds and 64 logical tasks
mirror_coordinate: one Givens angle modulating the second TT core per task
controls: LoRETTA-style shared outer cores plus independent task-specific middle TT core
shared TT core plus Mirror angle codes
generic rank-2 PCA factorization of middle TT cores

development.selection_metric: matrix/function NRMSE, actual serialized fp16 bytes, code fitting wall time

storage.authority: actual serialized inference payload bytes after deterministic fp16 decode
paid_objects: independent task TT cores or Mirror angles

success_gate: Aligned function NRMSE <=0.01 and at least 20% fewer bytes than LoRETTA independent TT factors; generic PCA matching Mirror means no Mirror-specific result. Independent tasks test private-factor boundary.
failure_gate: Mirror misses aligned quality/storage gate or generic PCA matches/improves it; independent cores outperforming Mirror is the boundary condition.
boundaries: Aligned teacher is generated from the same Givens core action
No LoRETTA training or language-model task evidence
All serialized cores decoded from fp16 for evaluation
